title: Differences between Hereditary and Sporadic MSI Endometrial Cancer Using Whole Slide Imaging and Digital Pathology (HeSpEC-DIGITAL Study)
summary:
Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is a biologically and molecularly heterogeneous malignancy. A distinct subgroup consists of tumors exhibiting microsatellite instability (MSI), which can arise either from epigenetic alterations—specifically MLH1 promoter hypermethylation—or from mutations in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes. The latter may be associated with hereditary Lynch syndrome, among other conditions. Distinguishing between these tumor groups is crucial for molecular diagnostics and clinical classification.

The HeSpEC-DIGITAL study investigates clinical, histological, molecular, and epigenetic differences among these various forms of MSI endometrial carcinoma. To this end, routinely obtained histopathological tissue sections are digitized (creating whole-slide images, or WSIs) and analyzed using digital image analysis and artificial intelligence (AI). The study aims to determine whether AI-based methods can identify characteristic image patterns linked to specific molecular or epigenetic tumor properties, thereby enabling a distinction between sporadic MSI tumors and those caused by MMR gene alterations. Additionally, protein expression patterns and genome-wide DNA methylation profiles are being analyzed.

Furthermore, the study examines the consistency with which recommended Lynch syndrome screenings were performed in routine clinical practice for patients with endometrial carcinoma and how the application of these screenings has evolved over time. Another component of the study assesses whether digital pathology, AI, and DNA methylation profiles can help better distinguish between endometrial adenocarcinomas and cervical adenocarcinomas, particularly in diagnostically challenging cases.

This involves analyzing clinical data and existing tumor samples from patients who underwent surgery for endometrial carcinoma or cervical adenocarcinoma between 2015 and 2025. In addition, patients prospectively enrolled in the already approved COLLECT study are included. The study is non-interventional; no additional procedures or examinations are required for the patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who underwent surgery for EC and cervical adenocarcinoma between 2015 and 2025 will be included in the study. No exclusions will be made based on histologic subtype; all histotypes are eligible, including cervical
adenocarcinoma, endometrioid carcinoma, serous carcinoma, clear cell carcinoma, carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumor), undifferentiated or dedifferentiated carcinoma, and mixed histologies. There will be no exclusions based on disease stage, tumor grade, or molecular subtype. For newly enrolled patients, eligibility will be limited to patients aged 18 years or older who have provided written informed consent and are enrolled in the
prospective COLLECT (COmprehensive anaLysis of clinical and moLEcular features in gynecologiCal patients undergoing Treatment, S-304/2023) study will be included.
